title: Audio Lesson: Context Compaction
limitations: Generated from concept pages; not yet reviewed.
Content may drift from source; verify against current main.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Context windows are finite. When a long agent session accumulates thousands of tokens, something has to give. Context compaction is the answer — a multi-layer pipeline that reduces context size without losing critical information.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Layer one is lossless pruning. It removes duplicates and empty messages with zero information loss. If the same tool returned the same result twice, the second copy is replaced with a pointer to the first. No LLM call needed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Layer two is structured distillation. It truncates very long messages, keeping the first and last portions with an ellipsis in the middle. A recovery pointer lets you retrieve the full original later.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Layer three is lossy LLM summarization. Older messages are summarized while recent ones are kept intact. A circuit breaker limits how many times this runs — if context is still too large after three cycles, the breaker trips rather than burning tokens endlessly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Users control this with chat commands. Slash-compact forces compaction. Slash-clear removes everything except system messages. Slash-resume creates a branch from a previous session point and continues from there.
